critical_code_review_comments: _compute_earnings loads orders with .to_list(50000) — a hard cap that will silently truncate at scale. For an analytics endpoint consider Mongo aggregation pipeline ($match → $group on driver_id with $sum) instead of in-process Python aggregation; both faster and avoids the 50k ceiling.

_order_eff_date slices ISO string with [:10] which assumes the date is stored as a string. If delivered_at/updated_at are ever stored as native datetime (e.g., from datetime.now() without isoformat()), the slice would silently return a wrong substring (e.g., '2026-01-13' vs 'datetime.d'). Add isinstance check or normalize at write time.

Date filter is inclusive on both ends via string comparison on YYYY-MM-DD; works fine for the current ISO-string storage but couples query semantics to storage format. Document this or move to true date-range Mongo query.

finances_export calls finances_summary(...) directly as a function — fine, but it passes current_user explicitly which bypasses Depends. Acceptable internal call pattern but worth a comment so future refactors don't accidentally enforce Depends twice.
Frontend finance-rate input has no client-side guard against negative / >100; backend accepts any float. Low-risk (admin-only) but worth bounding to [0, 1] server-side.

CSV filename in Response uses datetime.now(timezone.utc) — good (UTC, no locale). However the per-row Ingresos/Comision are written as raw floats — Excel locales using comma as decimal separator will parse '70.0' fine but '€' is not in the CSV (only in UI). Acceptable.

PATCH /orders/{id}/status sets delivered_at only if not previously set (idempotent) — good. But the endpoint has no role check; any authenticated user (customer included) can mark any order delivered. Out of scope for this iteration but a high-severity authz gap worth flagging.
Carry-over: AdminDashboard.js is 634 lines and growing; the finance section (~80 lines) could be extracted to a FinancePanel component for maintainability.
